links.comparator_used: Standalone sparse (BM25) retrieval and standalone dense (bi-encoder) retrieval
links.outcome: Retrieval and extraction performance in clinical NER (agitation in dementia, malnutrition risk factors), including item-level accuracy
links.effect: Reranking and hybrid ensemble strategies significantly outperformed standalone BM25 and dense retrieval on both tasks (repeated-measures ANOVA). For malnutrition, ensemble methods gave the best Item-level Accuracy (0.944).
links.quote: A repeated-measures ANOVA reveals that reranking and hybrid ensemble strategies significantly outperform both standalone sparse (BM25) and dense retrieval across both tasks.

links.comparator_used: Dense retrieval without cross-encoder reranking, and sparse BM25 retrieval
links.outcome: Answer F1, context diversity and item-level accuracy for agitation extraction
links.effect: Dense reranking achieved Answer F1 0.946, Context Diversity 0.895 and Item-level Accuracy 0.963 for agitation. For malnutrition, dense reranking was close behind the ensemble methods on Item-level Accuracy (best 0.944).
links.quote: For agitation extraction, Dense reranking achieves the highest Answer F1 (0.946), Context Diversity (0.895) and Item-level Accuracy (0.963).
